title: The Country Club Mindset
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article investigates why member-oriented clubs and associations are so often poorly managed compared to businesses and other nonprofits, rejecting governance structure alone as the explanation. It argues the deeper cause is a "Country Club" mindset, where member satisfaction becomes the sole operating criterion, pulling leaders toward short-term, reactive decision-making rather than vision-driven strategy. The piece contrasts this with customer-centric organizations that also prioritize satisfaction but build it on a foundation of explicit vision, goals, strategy, and process. It offers a practical diagnostic, asking a club for its vision, goals, strategies, and processes in sequence, to reveal whether an organization is genuinely being led or merely catering to members.
points: Poor management in member clubs is attributed less to governance structure and more to a "Country Club" mindset that treats member satisfaction as the sole operating criterion.
Prioritizing member happiness without an underlying vision produces a relaxed but under-directed environment where productivity suffers.
Successful customer-centric organizations also prioritize satisfaction, but build it on explicit vision, goals, strategy, and process rather than instinct alone.
A practical diagnostic, asking to see the vision, goals, strategies, and execution processes in sequence, reveals whether a club is actually being led.
quotes: Why are so many clubs, volunteer organizations, and member-centric associations so poorly run?
This means leaders take on a “Country Club” mindset, whereby anything that is not immediately connected to member satisfaction is given little attention.
The result is a relaxed and sometimes fun work environment where productivity suffers from a lack of direction and oversight.
Ask your club for the overall vision of the institution and the visions of each department.
Just because it’s a member club doesn’t mean it has to be led ineffectively.
